_about: All words in Euphemia Haynes, Lesson II: what is spoken and what appears on screen.
Edit text here; haynes_movement2.py and generate_movement2_audio.py both read this file.
After changing any 'narration', rerun generate_movement2_audio.py to rebuild the audio.
Narration may be one string or a list of sentences (they are joined with spaces).

The animation waits for some sentences to be spoken before showing what they describe; it finds them by the words in the 'cue' entries below, so keep each cue word-for-word the same as in the narration.
Count labels like "cusps {cusps}" get their numbers from haynes_curves.py, which computes them from Haynes's curve.

m2_11_duality: A curve can be seen in two ways: as a path of points, or as the family of lines that touch it.
Here is the three-cuspided quartic from Haynes's thesis.
Roll a tangent line around it, and record each line as a single point.
Those points draw a second curve, the dual.
Each cusp becomes a point of inflection.
And the one line that touches the quartic twice, at two invisible complex points, becomes a lone isolated point.
Its shape moves, but its counts do not.
Degree, cusps, and bitangents, with their partners in the dual, stay fixed.
Haynes described invariance as that which remains stable in midst of change.
m2_closing_simson: Return to the right triangle with sides three, four, and five.
Pick any point on the circle through its corners, and drop perpendiculars to the three sides.
The three feet always fall on a single line, called the Simson line.
As the point travels once around the circle, its Simson lines sweep out a curve.
It is the same three-cuspided quartic.
Classroom geometry and thesis geometry turn out to be one structure.
m2_closing_door: Haynes found another picture of what teaching aims for in the idea of a limit.
A polygon inscribed in a circle, with more and more sides, comes ever closer to the circle.
It never quite arrives, yet every step brings it nearer.
This gives us a visual metaphor for the larger promise of education: knowledge can open paths that were previously closed.
Mathematics can become an open door.
